adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:27 — deleteCache wipes CalendarCache rows but leaves googleChannelId/expiration set, and a cache miss in getFreeBusyResult never writes back, so the cache stays empty and every availability check hits Google live until an unrelated webhook fires.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `deleteCache.handler.ts` only deletes rows from `prisma.calendarCache` by `credentialId`; there is no `googleChannelId` field on `CalendarCache` (it exists on `SelectedCalendar`, which is unrelated to this delete). Also, the shown `GoogleCalendarService` logic explicitly repopulates the cache on a miss: after `fetchAvailability(parsedArgs)` it calls `setAvailabilityInCache(parsedArgs, data)`, contradicting the claim that a cache miss “never writes back” and would keep the cache empty until a webhook fires. Any interaction with webhook state/expiration is not evidenced in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:28 — Handler instantiates the concrete CalendarCacheRepository directly, bypassing the team-level "calendar-cache" feature gate, so leftover rows show as a healthy "Cache Status" (and a delete action) for users whose cache is disabled and never served.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, the handler directly does `const cacheRepository = new CalendarCacheRepository();` and then queries `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(...)`. The diff also shows a `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` whose methods explicitly log “Skipping ... due to calendar-cache being disabled”, implying there is (elsewhere) a feature-gated mechanism to swap implementations when the calendar-cache feature is disabled. Instantiating the concrete repository in the handler bypasses any such injection/switching, which could lead to cache status being returned based on leftover DB rows even when the feature is disabled. The diff doesn’t prove the feature gate wiring, so this is best treated as an architecture/scope concern rather than a definitively verifiable runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:42 — deleteCache mutation does not invalidate viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars (unlike the disconnect mutation), so after a successful delete the UI keeps showing the old "Last updated" timestamp and delete action unless the optional onChanged prop happens to refetch.

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx`, `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess?.()`; it does not invalidate any TRPC query cache. By contrast, `disconnectMutation` explicitly invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (and integrations) in `onSettled`. Since `cacheUpdatedAt` is sourced from `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (see `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` enriching the query result), deleting rows in `calendarCache` via `viewer.calendars.deleteCache` will leave the cached query data (and thus the displayed “Last updated” value / delete action visibility) stale unless the parent happens to refetch via `onSuccess`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:175 — Cache status takes max(updatedAt) over all rows for the credential with no expiresAt or current-key filter, so one fresh row (or rows for old month windows or deselected calendars) makes the status look healthy while the keys actually queried miss.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` uses `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy({ by: ["credentialId"], _max: { updatedAt: true } })` and does not filter by `expiresAt` or by any specific cache `key`. That means the UI field `cacheUpdatedAt` added in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` can reflect the most recently updated cache row for a credential even if the rows actually used for current availability lookups are expired or for different keys/calendars. This is a diff-grounded potential accuracy/UX issue, but the diff does not define the intended semantics of “Cache Status/Last updated”, so it’s not provably a functional defect from the PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/migrations/20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql:9 — Backfilling updatedAt with DEFAULT NOW() stamps every legacy, possibly stale, cache row as freshly updated at migration time, so the UI reports false freshness.

adjudication.rationale: The migration adds a NOT NULL `updatedAt` with `DEFAULT NOW()` (migration.sql + schema.prisma `@default(now()) @updatedAt`). `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` then surfaces cache freshness via `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` which returns `_max.updatedAt`, and the new UI (`CredentialActionsDropdown`) displays it as “Last updated”. For pre-existing CalendarCache rows, the migration will set `updatedAt` to the migration time regardless of when the cache value was actually produced, so the UI can indeed report misleadingly fresh timestamps for legacy/stale cache entries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1024 — Every webhook refill now runs an extra updateMany with empty data on SelectedCalendar whose updatedAt is never consumed by the UI (status comes from CalendarCache), and a failure there fails the webhook after the cache write already succeeded.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` in `CalendarService.ts` after writing availability to cache. This is an `updateMany` call with an empty `data` object (passed through to `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: { credentialId }, data })`). That does not actually “Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt” as the comment claims (no fields are set), and depending on Prisma/runtime validation may throw, which would cause the webhook refill to fail after the cache write has already succeeded. The UI cache status shown in this diff is sourced from `CalendarCache.updatedAt` (`connectedCalendars.handler.ts` enriches `cacheUpdatedAt` via `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), so this extra update is at best ineffective and at worst a failing no-op.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:24 — Missing or foreign credential throws a plain Error instead of a TRPCError NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN, so it surfaces as a 500 and can't be told apart from real server failures.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:25 — New deleteCache mutation throws a plain Error for missing/unauthorized credential, which tRPC surfaces as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) instead of a TRPCError NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN, so clients cannot distinguish auth failure from server fault.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`, the handler checks credential ownership and, if missing/unauthorized, does `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` (around the `if (!credential)` block). In tRPC, throwing a plain `Error` is typically serialized as an `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` rather than a typed `TRPCError` (e.g., `NOT_FOUND`/`FORBIDDEN`), so clients can’t reliably distinguish auth/ownership failure from a server fault. This incorrect error classification/contract is introduced by the new mutation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts:23 — Exported UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId on allSelectedCalendars/userLevelSelectedCalendars even though the function never reads them, forcing every external caller (e.g. platform/api-v2 via platform-libraries) to widen its select or fail to compile.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the exported `UserWithCalendars` type in `packages/lib/getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts` to include `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` in the `Pick<SelectedCalendar,...>` for both `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars`. That is a potentially breaking type-level API change for any external caller that uses `UserWithCalendars` (or constructs values matching it) and didn’t previously select/provide those fields. The diff itself doesn’t prove which external packages are impacted, but the type signature change is real and not a runtime defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:28 — connectedCalendars instantiates the concrete CalendarCacheRepository instead of going through ICalendarCacheRepository selection, so the new mock getCacheStatusByCredentialIds is dead and the cacheUpdatedAt output field is populated even when calendar-cache is disabled.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, the diff explicitly imports and instantiates the concrete `CalendarCacheRepository` (`new CalendarCacheRepository()`), rather than obtaining an `ICalendarCacheRepository` via some selector/factory. That does make the new mock method `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` unused by this code path and increases coupling/limits testability and configurability. However, the claim that this causes `cacheUpdatedAt` to be populated “even when calendar-cache is disabled” cannot be verified from the diff alone because no feature-flag/selection mechanism is shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/platform/atoms/selected-calendars/wrappers/SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx:130 — Error-state (Alert) branch now honors disableConnectionModification, silently removing the disconnect action for atom consumers that previously could still remove a broken credential with that prop set.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change behavior in the error-state actions branch: previously the Alert/error card showed `DisconnectIntegration` whenever `!connectedCalendar.delegationCredentialId` (ignoring `disableConnectionModification`). Now it always renders `CredentialActionsDropdown`, which internally computes `canDisconnect = !delegationCredentialId && !disableConnectionModification` and returns `null` if neither disconnect nor cache actions are allowed. This means consumers passing `disableConnectionModification={true}` will no longer see a disconnect/remove action in the error-state path where they previously did. Whether that’s intended is a product/API contract question rather than a clearly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:25 — Missing/unauthorized credential throws a plain Error, surfacing as a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a TRPCError NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `deleteCache.handler.ts`, the code checks ownership via `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })` and, when not found, throws a plain `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. In a tRPC mutation (added in `_router.tsx`), an untyped Error will typically be converted to an `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` rather than a more appropriate `NOT_FOUND`/`FORBIDDEN` TRPCError, so the finding is grounded in the diff and represents incorrect error signaling for an authorization/not-found condition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:174 — Cache status groupBy ignores expiresAt, so credentials whose cache rows are all expired (and never served) still report a "Last updated" cache status

adjudication.rationale: The new `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` uses `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy({ where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds } }, _max: { updatedAt: true } })` and does not filter out expired rows via `expiresAt`. The connected calendars handler then surfaces this as `cacheUpdatedAt` and the UI displays “Last updated”. If all cache rows for a credential are expired but still present in the table, the feature will still report a cache “Last updated” timestamp even though there is no valid cache to serve.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:42 — deleteCache onSuccess never invalidates connectedCalendars (unlike the disconnect mutation), so when onChanged is not passed the stale cache status and delete action remain visible

adjudication_records.issue_text: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:33 — Script trusts a predictable, world-writable /tmp/tmole.log (and reuses any running "tmole 3000" process) as the source of GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL, so another local user can plant a tunnel URL and redirect Google webhook traffic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:6 — Greedy `https://.*\.tunnelmole\.net` regex can capture arbitrary log text, which is then written unescaped into the sed replacement and .env file.

adjudication.rationale: In scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh, TM_KEYWORD is set to the greedy regex `https://.*\.tunnelmole\.net` and used with `grep -oE` to extract `$TUNNEL_URL` from the log. Because `.*` is greedy, it can match beyond the actual URL if the log line contains additional text before the final `.tunnelmole.net`, producing an overlong/tainted `$TUNNEL_URL`. That value is then interpolated unescaped into the `sed` replacement (`...GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=$TUNNEL_URL...`) and appended to the .env file, which can lead to incorrect .env contents or sed replacement issues if the match contains unexpected characters.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/migrations/20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql:9 — Backfilling updatedAt with DEFAULT NOW() makes legacy cache rows look freshly updated at migration time, and nothing validates the migration or the displayed status for pre-existing rows.

adjudication.rationale: The migration adds `CalendarCache.updatedAt` as `NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()` (and Prisma marks it `@default(now()) @updatedAt`). This will stamp all pre-existing `CalendarCache` rows with the migration execution time, even though their cached contents may be old. The new UI/server logic then displays cache freshness via `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` using `_max.updatedAt` and surfaces it as `cacheUpdatedAt` in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, so legacy rows will appear “freshly updated” immediately after migration. The diff shows no compensating backfill based on real cache recency (e.g., existing timestamps) or handling to mark legacy rows as unknown/stale, making the finding verifiable from the diff.
